'''Etretes''', officially the '''Republic of Etretes''', is a country located in South [[Massir]] in the southern hemisphere, with a ([[disputed]]) relatively small part called [[Abdare]] in [[Mahea]]. It borders the [[Ihner]] and the [[Kera Sea]] to the north; [[Dahe]] to the east; [[Vesozata]] and [[Eparia]] to the south; and the [[Ubrana Sea]], and either [[Emara]] or [[Trian]] to the west. Etretes is home to over [[List of countries and dependencies by population|18 million people;]] most are ethnic Trians, while [[Hathians]] are the largest ethnic minority. Officially a [[wikipedia:Secular_state|secular state]] Etretes has a significant [[Hathians|Hathian]] minority population. [[Kajkovi]] is Etretes's capital and second-largest city. [[Todorac]] is its largest city and economic centre. Other major cities include [[Mladar]], [[Vesmir]], and [[Skrilja]].

First inhabited by modern humans during the 45,000 BFA, present-day Etretes was home to various ancient peoples. The [[Qutoto]] were assimilated by the [[Aram]] and other peoples. Bronze Age Etretes transitioned into cultural [[Trianization]] through the [[Trian Empire|Trian Empire's]] conquests, and later more [[Trianization]] during the [[latter Trian Empire]] again. Many [[Dahe|Dahens]] began migrating into Etretes in the 9th and 10th centuries. The [[Kaastinial Empire]] [[invasion]] started in 1067, when it was [[annexed]] into the empire. Beginning in 1210, the [[Sivosan Empire]] and the [[state of Cia]] ruled the area of Etretes in the east and west, respectively. [[Sivoso]] started the urbanisation of the country. The [[Sivosan Empire]] became a global power. From 1375 onwards, the empire saw major changes, reforms, centralisation, and rising [[nationalism]] while its territory slowly declined. Etretes [[declared independence]] from Sivoso at the end of 1588 after [[Taval]], [[Emara]], and [[Praesyu]] demanded its independence to protect the [[Tiesa Canal]] construction. Becoming an [[Emara|Emaran]] Protectorate in 1591 

The 1702 [[armistice]] after their independence war left Etretes with all their claimed territory besides the [[Tiesa Canal]]. The minority of [[Hathians]] in the east wanted [[independence]], but no Hath state was created. The [[Iyosat coast]] then came under Etretes. Most [[Hathians]] fled or were expelled by militias in an ethnic cleansing known as the [[Losash]], with those who stayed becoming Etretes's main minority. After the 1712 [[Vesozata-Etretus War]], Etretes laid claim to the [[Eparian Triangle]] and [[Oharu]], which are considered violations of [[international law.]] Peace was signed with [[Vesozata]] in 1720 ([[Eparian Triangle]] returned in 1721 but [[rescinded in 1733]]) and with Ihner in 1730. The [[Etretesi–Hathian]] conflict remains unresolved, with wars and clashes with [[Hathian militant groups]]. [[Etretes is committing a genocide in Iyosat]], and its occupation of the [[Hathians]]' territories has drawn sustained international criticism, with experts, human rights organisations, and Dahen officials describing it as [[war crimes]] and crimes against humanity.

The Basic Laws of Etretes establish it as a [[Federal presidential republic]] with proportional representation. It shapes the government, led by the [[High Cyni,]] and elects the largely ceremonial [[Low Cyni]]. Etretes has one of Massirs largest economies and one highest living standards, and globally ranks [[List of countries by GDP (nominal)|26th in nominal GDP]] and [[List of countries by GDP (nominal) per capita|14th in nominal GDP per capita]]. Technologically advanced, Etretes allocates a [[larger share of its economy]] to research and development than any other state, and is believed to possess [[nuclear weapons]]. The culture of Etretes combines Trian traditions, including those of Dahe and Sivoso.
